newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude firmer, worries over Minas/Duri stocks.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude firmer, worries over Minas/Duri stocks.

text.p: Asian crude prices were firmer on Friday but differentials made little headway as MidEast trading came towards an end and regional players remained worried about stocks of Minas and Duri.
A European major has offloaded significant amounts of MidEast grades in the last few days, including Murban and Lower Zakum.
Traders said the major sold one million barrels of Murban to a U.S. major, although the U.S. major would not confirm. Traders said the U.S. major had said it bought a "small piece" of Murban.
However, traders were worried the volume would overhang the market and undermine pricing of remaining March availabilities.
Two U.S. majors have moved two million barrels of Minas, Duri and Widuri into their own systems in the USWC.
Another parcel of 600,000 barrels of Minas may have traded into China in recent days, traders said. They assessed Minas at ICP -30/40, slightly up from ICP -50 last done.
Duri was assessed at ICP -30 cents, in line with the last done, although sellers were talking nearer flat.
